# Home Environment Manager v0.6.0b47 - Valid-only sensor means and mold recalibration

## What was wrong

When more than one temperature, humidity, pressure or other numerical input was selected for a room, one unavailable or stale source could invalidate the entire reading. The per-room mold recalibration button separately insisted on one previously pinned temperature sensor. With two or more properly selected room temperature sensors this caused Home Assistant to report: "Mold temperature source is not selected for this room".

## Fixed: mean from valid measurements

Numerical inputs of the **same physical metric** now contribute a simple arithmetic mean after Home Assistant entity normalization and unit conversion. Sources in `unknown`, `unavailable`, stale, non-numeric, not finite, invalid units/ranges, assigned to a different room, or generated by the Manager are excluded from the mean. A group with one valid value returns that value; a group with no valid readings remains unavailable. Nothing is silently replaced with zero or readings from an unselected room.

The same approach applies to selected room temperature, humidity, pressure, normalized room air-quality readings including CO2 and particulate matter, outdoor numerical weather and pollution observations, the deterministic ventilation threshold evaluation, climate-controller feedback, physics history and the dashboard data. The verified rejected-source list remains available in temperature diagnostic evidence. Individually unavailable outdoor sensor identifiers remain tracked.

This does not average categorical states: rain, storm alerts, unsafe weather descriptions, actual window contacts, presence and safety interlocks retain their own logic. AQI scales are intentionally not combined across incompatible providers.

## Mold calibration button

The room calibration button now obtains the mean of **all valid temperature sensors selected in Room Setup**. An old single-sensor pin no longer blocks a multi-selected room. A room with one legacy explicitly pinned source still works as before. It similarly averages valid temperatures from configured weather sources. The button saves the full input-source lists and exact calibrated indoor/outdoor means. Those values appear as attributes on the button, alongside the existing measured coldest wall-surface temperature and factor.

A changed set of selected sources invalidates the previously calculated factor rather than continuing to use the old factor for new input geometry; transient unavailability does not invalidate a selection. Manual calibration still requires an actual coldest-surface measurement, valid indoor/outdoor temperature contrast and physical factor limits. If calibration fails, the prior stored good factor and its metadata are not overwritten.

## Compatibility and installation

This is the opt-in canonical `environment_manager` beta only. All Beta46 typography improvements, Beta45 cover selection and independent cover controls, previous controller functionality and protections remain. No automatic equipment authorization, sensor enrollment, firmware command, window movement or migration is added. Older released tags and stable **v0.5.1** are not changed.

In Home Assistant HACS, open Home Environment Manager -> Redownload / version selection -> Show beta versions -> select **v0.6.0b47** -> restart Home Assistant. Revisit Room Setup to ensure the intended room temperature, humidity and air-quality sensors are selected. Use the per-room mold calibration button again if a temperature/weather source list was edited, because a factor tied to the previous source set must not be reused.

## Validation gates

Publication requires the full Python 3.13 and 3.14 suite (including valid-only means, unit conversion and the mold button), frontend Node checks, regenerated 38-language catalogs, syntax, HACS/hassfest checks, Home Assistant 2026.10 registry and controller smoke tests, and exact flat HACS archive install simulation. The prerelease is created only after those gates pass.
